key_insight: 3D coupled opto-electro-thermal simulations show that lead-free MgXS3 (X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites can achieve high-efficiency solar cells when thickness, doping, defect density, and an Sb2S3 BSF layer are optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design guidance for building thermally robust, lead-free photovoltaic stacks with realistic 3D performance and heat-management considerations.
method: Self-consistent coupling of optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer
Systematic sweep of absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and BSF effect
evidence_signal: Optimized devices reached simulated efficiencies of 28.18% (MgZrS3), 26.72% (MgTiS3), and 28.16% (MgHfS3), with corresponding VOC, JSC, and FF values reported in the abstract.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, so experimental validation and fabrication tolerance under real interfaces, defects, and thermal cycling remain necessary.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
